Can never find topic that is advertised when I click your push notifications. [Updating a previous very positive review now that my count of devotions heard is up to over 700…(1), I have in 2026 and today still, 4/28/26 been having a problem a year that an interesting sounding push notification topic comes up on my iPhone 16e, but when I follow it, it leads to a menu of devotions, and week long study series, none of which are the subject teased in the notification Can you have it link directly to the devotion it is advertising? Or at least allow us to search your crammed-full menu? I have a Bible reading plan with my paper Bible I’m lucky to keep up, so I don’t use the “sign up for a week of …” come-ons, really. So my use of the app has fallen significantly though I’m still paying for it, hopefully someone else is gaining satisfaction from the typically well done meditations. Though the breathing and relaxation really doesn’t suit me if I listen in the AM, and I find it all kinda “new age” 

Previous review: Have just lost a paper journal yet again in my house, so the times I’ve “written in my journal” here are also of importance in the wee hours, not bedtime, when I can contemplate & have energy to write at the same time. Have copied some to notes in my iPhone, which I’ve had one of for almost a decade - so maybe more secure than paper? For now anyway. 
(2) Just having listened to the Jenn Stoltzfus / Tyler Bods “I am Loved” devotion, I used it as springboard, with a screenshot of your starry night graphic, on FB, having recalled my Dad using that phrase (1) time to me in my life (we were not a family where “I love you” was said, ever, either: though a good upbringing otherwise.) My suggestion: one problem I have in the Roman’s 8:35-39 journey, which is likely all of our lifetime journals, to see if God ever leaves us, is not the danger / deprivation / illness / storms struggle, nor the power of angels or anything created, except MYSELF. Perhaps it shows narcissism but that scripture leaves put one created thing which I constantly fear WILL show God will or has left me or that I’ve been fooling myself I’m loved: MY OWN FAILURE, amplified by Satan’s semi-true or true accusations… Perhaps a devotion where the pilgrim passes THAT created hurdle would be good. Yeah, I know Paul did address it when he said he was the “chiefest of sinners” but I think we are all, in our failures, and disappointments in ourselves, capable of feeling we are a special case, and even “Chiefer” than Paul… I bet some devotions of this nature will be coming ! You demonstrate God’s power & constancy very well of COURSE. Thanks again

THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT TIME FOR PEOPLE TO GET A GOOD WORD AND ALL IF THE INCREDIBLE THINGS THIS APP OFFERS with Bible verses and encouragements etc. but now because MOST OF THE WORLD CANNOT AFFORD EXTRAS LIKE THIS, we get barely any use of the app now?!?! I lost my husband to a particularly horrific cancer December 8 of last year. He was a true evangelist and a pastor for the last 17 years of his life. 

I affectionately called my husband “Superman”. He was physically strong and so brave. I always felt safe when I was with him. He was also a wonderful provider. He was my best friend and my partner. We shared a deeply intense love from the moment almost that we met. I was only 16 and I am now 55. 

The most wonderful thing about my husband was his love for Jesus. He encountered Jesus in his 30’s and was made a new creation. 2 Corinthians 5:17 was his life verse because of the radical change Jesus made in his life. 
 
My husband grew up horrifically abused in every way imaginable. He was abandoned by his biological father and as he used to say, his mother married a man who hated children and she had six of them. He began using alcohol around the age of 12 to numb the pain of the abuse he was living in. He became emotionally shut off and developed a very tough exterior. 

He ran away at 15 and slept under bridges and lived house to house with everyone from his older sister to a motorcycle gang. He survived by becoming an entrepreneur and a great salesman. 

My husband loved kids and the elderly. He would step in without hesitation to protect anyone being abused or attacked. He was a fighter. However, when he accepted Jesus as his Lord and Savior, that tough exterior became a welcoming smile and caring heart. 

In January of 2020, my mothers suffered a complete mental breakdown, that affected her physically and mentally, to the point that my Dad could no longer care for her by himself. My husband insisted they move in with us. My husband and I stayed in a camper in our driveway and my parents lived in our home for 15 months, while we built an apartment for them onto the rear of our home. 

July of 2020, my husband saw an ENT because his throat had been bothering him. Antibiotics had not helped and it felt like something was stuck in the right side of his throat. Due to COVID, I was waiting in the parking garage of Emory Midtown Hospital, in downtown Atlanta, Georgia, when my husband called and asked me to come into the hospital. 

When I walked into the office that my husband directed me to, I didn’t notice that the sign in the hallway said, Emory Winship Head and Neck Clinic. The ENT had immediately recognized the place in my husband’s throat as a cancerous tumor. He walked him over to the Head and Neck clinic and got them to work him in. When I saw my husband and I sat down next to him, he looked at me and said, “Hey Steph, I’ve got cancer.” Even now those words and the constant flurry of radiation, chemo, surgery, doctor visits, ambulance rides, and emergency hospital admissions, that finally concluded in a hospice room at 8:05 pm on December 8, 2022, seem unreal and incomprehensible! It was utter chaos. 

The chaos did not stop on December 8th. I became the sole provider for myself. A role I have never experienced. I worked on and off during my 37 year marriage but only doing things I loved, as I had opportunity. Any income I made typically went toward extras for our girls or Christmas for our grands, when they came along, trips, etc. 

I had acquired a part time job, the Spring of 2021, working in our local Baptist Association as the Administrative Assistant. My husband seemed to be winning his cancer battle at that time and he wanted me to have something to distract me from all we were going through (I believe he was helping prepare me just in case) I was also working as a Counseling Intern to obtain the supervised hours required for my certification as an Addictions Counselor (this was also at the urging of my husband). Helping addicted people confront the real issue and discover their true needs that can only be met by God is my passion and my husband pushed me to continue even though he was sick and I wanted to be with him every minute of the day. In October of 2022, I tested and passed my certification test to become a CACI in Georgia. My husband had been in and out of the hospital but he insisted I keep the appointment for my test so some friends came and sat with him, while I went. That’s the kind of man he was. He put the needs of others before himself. 

Now I am still battling the overwhelming waves of grief as I try to navigate moving into full time employment, while still helping to care for my parents and take care of all the home maintenance and repairs that my husband did himself. 

Thank you for what Abide has provided today. To hear the Words of God related to my circumstances that remind me of the hope that we have in Jesus.
